provenance.instrument: Southampton Township Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 39 Zoning, Ord. No. 2017-002 of 4-25-2017, as amended), as published on Municode
provenance.status_detail: Municode Library, Southampton Township, Franklin County (the code's own title). District use lists and the minimum area tables are text in Parts 7 to 11. Floodplain rules are in Chapter 10, Floodplain Management Ordinance. The township's codes page links only to Municode and to Ord. No. 2021-003 (solar)
provenance.code_current_through_note: Municode version 'Dec 23, 2024 (Current)': 'Codified through Ordinance No. 2024-002, enacted October 22, 2024. (Supp. No. 3)'
checks: ECHO housing (Elder Cottage Housing Opportunities), 'also known as granny flat or elder cottage housing': accessory to the house, one or two bedrooms, connected to the house's utilities, and either transportable manufactured housing without a permanent foundation or the residential conversion of an existing accessory structure (Part 14 'ECHO Housing'). Permitted by right in A, R-1 and R-2 (39-321A)

ECHO standards: at most two stories and 900 sq ft of total floor area, one per lot, combined building coverage within the district maximum, occupied by an elderly, handicapped or disabled person related to the occupants of the house by blood, marriage or adoption, at most two people, connected to the house's utilities, no added parking when the house meets its own, not in the required front yard and within the side and rear yards for principal uses, an open covered walkway to the house allowed. The right to occupy ends on the death or relocation of the family member or the sale of the property, and the unit is removed (or a converted accessory structure restored) within 90 days. A letter of determination from the Zoning Officer comes before the land use and building permits (39-321A(1) to (12))

Two-family detached dwellings (one unit over the other) are permitted by right in R-2 and C on a lot 25% larger than the single-family minimum. Conversion of an existing single-family dwelling into a two-family dwelling is permitted by right in R-2 and a conditional use in C, with two entrances per unit, two parking spaces per unit and lot area of the single-family minimum plus 3,000 sq ft per added unit (39-901B, E, 39-1001B, 39-1002A)

Semi-detached dwellings (duplex) are permitted in R-2 and C and a conditional use in R-1. Individual mobile homes are permitted in A and R-1 as a principal dwelling (39-701D, 39-801G, 39-802G, 39-901C, 39-1001C)
During construction of a single-family house one mobile home or travel trailer may be lived in for six months, once extendable for six more (39-306A)

Accessory buildings: at most 25 ft tall, they meet the yard rules (a nonpermanent one of 200 sq ft or less and one story may be 5 ft from side and rear lines), together cover at most 30% of the required rear or side yard, and stand no nearer the street than the house's setback (39-300)
An existing small lot may be used if it meets all district rules other than lot area, width and side yards, with side yards of 8 ft and rear yards of 10 ft (39-302D)

Floodplain (Chapter 10): new construction or substantial improvement of a residential structure in the identified floodplain must have its lowest floor 1.5 ft above the 100-year flood elevation. Manufactured homes are prohibited in the floodway and within 50 ft landward of the top of bank in the other floodplain areas, and where permitted in any floodplain area they must be placed on a permanent foundation. Other new construction within 50 ft landward of the top of bank needs a permit from the Department of Environmental Protection. An accessory structure skips the elevation rule only if it is not used for human habitation (10-402.3B, 4B, 10-404.1, 10-404.4, 10-407.1 to 10-407.3)

Parking: at least two spaces for each dwelling unit, three where more than two unrelated persons live in it. A garage or carport counts, and a front-yard driveway of a one- or two-family house counts as up to two (39-304A, B)

Commercial district: a single apartment combined with a permitted commercial use in a multiple use building, and conversion apartments combined with a commercial use, are conditional uses (39-1002D, E)
C-I permits as accessory uses 'dwellings for bona fide caretakers or watchmen only' (39-1101S)

Buildings for seasonal laborers and similar farm employees and their families are permitted as an accessory use to agricultural operations, with a land use permit, and group quarters stand at least 500 ft from property lines (39-312)

Variances: the Zoning Hearing Board on the findings of 39-603C(a) to (e). No bar on a use variance was found. A nonconforming use may not be enlarged by more than 50% without the Board's approval (39-400C)

The R-2 table heads its lot figures 'Minimum required for single-family detached dwellings (minimum required for each dwelling unit)'. If an ECHO unit counts as a dwelling unit, a lot with public water and sewer needs 17,000 sq ft for the house and the unit (39-903B)

term.note: 'also known as granny flat or elder cottage housing. ECHO housing permits a family member, related by blood, marriage or adoption, to live independently but close to relatives on the same lot'

status.note: 'Within the (A), (R-1), and (R-2) districts ECHO housing is permitted by right, as an accessory use to a principal single-family residence'. Only an elderly, handicapped or disabled relative of the occupants of the house

status_outside.note: C and C-I do not list ECHO housing

path.note: Permitted by right. A written letter of determination from the Zoning Officer comes before the land use permit and building permit

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board on the findings of 39-603C(a) to (e). No bar on a use variance was found

value.name: Conversion of a single-family dwelling into a two-family dwelling (R-2)
value.conditions: Conversion apartments: an existing single-family detached dwelling converted into a two-family dwelling, each unit with two points of entrance and exit and two off-street parking spaces. Lot area of the single-family minimum plus 3,000 sq ft for each added unit, and the single-family setbacks. Labor and Industry approval comes first where it applies
value.note: A house divided into two units, not a unit added to it. The lot figures add 3,000 sq ft to the 39-903B single-family minimum for each column

value.name: Conversion of a single-family dwelling into a two-family dwelling (C)
value.conditions: Conversion apartments: an existing single-family detached dwelling converted into a two-family dwelling, each unit with two points of entrance and exit and two off-street parking spaces. Lot area of the single-family minimum plus 3,000 sq ft for each added unit, and the single-family setbacks
value.note: A house divided into two units, not a unit added to it. C takes the single-family figures of Part 8

value.name: Two-family detached dwelling (R-2, C)
value.conditions: A building for two families with one unit over the other, on a lot 25% larger than the single-family minimum, meeting the single-family yards
value.note: A new two-unit building, not a unit added to a house. The figures are for a lot with centralized water and sewer

value.name: Dwelling for a caretaker or watchman (C-I)
value.conditions: An accessory use customarily incidental to a permitted C-I use, for bona fide caretakers or watchmen only

requires.condition: The lot holds a permitted C-I use and the dwelling houses its bona fide caretaker or watchman

value.note: Housing for a caretaker or watchman of a business, not a general ADU

value.name: Housing for seasonal and farm employees (A)
value.conditions: Buildings for seasonal laborers and similar farm employees and their families, as an accessory use to an agricultural operation, with a land use permit and federal and state approvals. Group quarters stand at least 500 ft from property lines

requires.condition: The lot is an agricultural operation and the occupants work on it

value.note: Housing for farm workers on a farm, not a general ADU. 39-312 reaches agricultural operations in any district that permits them. Only A was checked

building_types.note: 'as an accessory use to a principal single-family residence'. Part 14 names semi-detached and row houses single-family dwellings, so a twin or row house is read to qualify. The lot must still hold the unit within the yards and coverage

districts_read_no_listing.note: Neither lists ECHO housing. C-I permits dwellings for bona fide caretakers or watchmen only (39-1101S)

value.condition: The unit must be connected to the utility systems serving the house, with no separate systems. With on-site sewer or water the applicant shows the Board of Supervisors the systems can serve both units.

The right to occupy ends on the death or relocation of the family member or the sale of the property, whichever comes first. Within 90 days the unit is removed, or a converted accessory structure is restored to its previous condition.
The building coverage of the house, existing accessory structures and the ECHO unit together may not exceed the district maximum.

Where permitted within any floodplain area, all manufactured homes and any improvements to them must be placed on a permanent foundation, and manufactured homes are prohibited in the floodway. A new ECHO unit must be transportable manufactured housing used without a permanent foundation, so it cannot meet both rules anywhere in the identified floodplain.

In the general and special floodplain areas manufactured homes are prohibited within 50 ft landward of the top of bank of any watercourse. Other new construction or development there needs a permit from the Department of Environmental Protection.

Within any identified floodplain area, new construction or substantial improvement of a residential structure must have the lowest floor, including the basement, 1.5 ft above the 100-year flood elevation. An accessory structure skips this only if it is not used for human habitation, so a converted accessory structure used as an ECHO unit must be elevated when the work is a substantial improvement.

types_allowed.note: 'Units must be either transportable manufactured housing to be used without a permanent foundation, or the residential conversion of an existing accessory structure'

types_not_addressed.note: A unit in or added to the house is not named. A covered walkway may join the unit to the house 'without the unit being considered part of the principal residence'. Whether the upper floor of an existing garage counts as the conversion of an existing accessory structure is not settled

value.detached_new: transportable manufactured ECHO unit without a permanent foundation
value.garage_conversion: conversion of an existing accessory structure

max_sqft.note: 'The ECHO housing may not exceed two stories and 900 square feet of total floor area'

occupancy.value: An elderly, handicapped or disabled person related to the occupants of the house by blood, marriage or adoption, and at most two people. The right to occupy ends on that person's death or relocation or on the sale of the property.

max_adus.note: 'A limit of one ECHO housing unit is permitted per lot'

district_yards_bind_accessory.note: 'shall not be permitted in the required front yard setback and shall adhere to all side and rear yard setback requirements for principal uses'

accessory_structure_max_height_ft.note: An accessory building not attached to the house 'shall not be more than 25 feet in height'

accessory_cap_binds_adu.note: Whether the accessory building height reaches an ECHO unit is not settled. 39-321 sets two stories

spaces_required.note: 'No additional parking shall be required for an ECHO housing unit so long as the principal residence complies with prevailing Township parking requirements'

min_lot_sqft.note: Two acres. With on-lot sewage the minimum may be increased for health reasons

max_building_coverage.note: 'All buildings including accessory buildings shall not cover more than ten percent of the area of the lot.'
'All buildings including accessory buildings shall not cover more than 30 percent of the area of the lot.'

Other than central water and sewer: neither

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached with centralized water and sewer

max_building_coverage.note: 'All buildings including accessory buildings shall not cover more than 50 percent of the area of the lot.'
